subject.title: fix(snapshot): make SQLite publication crash recoverable

question: After the missing native Windows and exact-head cross-platform evidence is available, should snapshot commands fail on every non-Windows directory-sync error while treating only the documented Windows directory-flush limitations as unsupported?
rationale: This is an intentional reliability-versus-availability policy change in an existing backup and restore workflow; the implementation is plausible, but maintainers must confirm the supported-platform failure contract before merge.

options.title: Require platform proof before merge
options.body: Keep the strict contract and add exact-head native Windows plus broader supported-filesystem evidence for create, list, verify, and fresh restore.

options.title: Accept narrower proof
options.body: Merge after focused coverage only, accepting residual uncertainty about directory-sync behavior on supported Windows and POSIX filesystems.

recommendation.title: Require platform proof before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the strict contract and add exact-head native Windows plus broader supported-filesystem evidence for create, list, verify, and fresh restore.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and are assigned to the current durability implementation, and are best positioned to provide the missing platform evidence.
